summary.en: Salvadoran forces have begun airstrikes and ground assaults against Haitian gang leaders, targeting strongholds and resulting in gang casualties. Haitian police raids in Port-au-Prince have also eliminated suspected gang members, while two Salvadoran soldiers died while handling explosives during the operations. The UN chief condemned a recent attack that caused dozens of civilian deaths, and the EU imposed sanctions on four Haitian gangs for serious human rights violations. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske styrker har begynt luftangrep og bakkekamp mot haitiske gjengledere, og rammer deres festningsverk, noe som har ført til gjengtap. Haitisk politi har gjennomført razziaer i Port-au-Prince og tatt bort mistenkte gjengmedlemmer, mens to salvadoranske soldater døde da de håndterte sprengstoff under operasjonene. FN-sjefen fordømte et nylig angrep som forårsaket dusinvis av sivile dødsfall, og EU innførte sanksjoner mot fire haitiske gjenger for alvorlige brudd på menneskerettighetene. Konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
